s2.ptxt: Remove the oil filler cap from the cylinder head cover.
Remove the oil filler cap gasket from the oil filler cap.
Using a deep socket wrench (22mm), remove the ventilation valve from the cylinder head cover.
Remove the 4 spark plugs from the cylinder head.
Using SST, remove the oil filter.

atten4.ptxt: Prepare a drain pan in advance, as oil will drain out.

s2.ptxt: Using a 12 socket hexagon wrench, remove the oil filter union.
Remove the 8 bolts and 2 nuts, and remove the cylinder head cover.
Remove the cylinder head cover gasket from the cylinder head cover.
Remove the bolt and nut, and remove the V-belt tensioner assembly.
Remove the 2 bolts and clip, and remove the crankshaft position sensor.
Remove the 3 bolts and remove the engine mounting bracket RH from the timing chain cover.
Remove the bolt and remove the camshaft position sensor from the cylinder head.
Turn the crankshaft clockwise to set the No. No.1 cylinder to TDC/compression, and align the timing mark (notch) with the 0° position of the timing chain cover.
At this time, check that the timing marks of the camshaft timing gears and the bearing caps are in the positions shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: If the marks are not aligned, turn the crankshaft clockwise again and align the marks.

s2.ptxt: Using SST, hold the crankshaft pulley and loosen the pulley bolt.
Screw the pulley bolt 2-3 pitches into the crankshaft.
Using SST, remove the crankshaft pulley and pulley bolt.

atten4.ptxt: Apply lubricant to the threads and tip of the SST center bolt before use.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Camshaft Timing Oil Control Valve Assembly

s2.ptxt: Remove the bolt and remove the camshaft timing oil control valve assembly from the cylinder head.

atten3.ptxt: If the camshaft timing oil control valve is not removed, it may be damaged when loosening the cylinder head bolts.

s2.ptxt: Remove the 2 nuts, and remove the chain tensioner assembly No.1 and gasket.

atten3.ptxt: Never rotate the crankshaft with the chain tensioner removed.

s2.ptxt: Using SST, remove the water pump pulley.
Remove the 4 bolts and 2 nuts, and remove the water pump assembly and wire harness clamp bracket.
Using a screwdriver wrapped with protective tape, pry at the location shown in the illustration and remove the water pump assembly.
Remove the oil pan drain plug and gasket from the oil pan.
Remove the 12 bolts and 2 nuts.
Using an oil pan seal cutter, remove the oil pan.

atten3.ptxt: Do not damage the oil pan installation surface or the oil pan flange.

atten4.ptxt: Clean and inspect the bolts and stud bolts.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Timing Chain or Belt Cover Sub-assembly

s2.ptxt: Using a torx socket wrench (E10), remove the stud bolt.
Remove the 12 bolts and 2 nuts.
Using a screwdriver wrapped with protective tape, pry at the location shown in the illustration and remove the timing chain cover.

atten3.ptxt: Do not damage the timing chain cover, cylinder block or cylinder head.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Timing Gear Case or Timing Chain Case Oil Seal

s2.ptxt: Using a screwdriver wrapped with protective tape, remove the timing gear (chain) case oil seal.

atten3.ptxt: Do not damage the oil seal installation surface.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Crank Angle Sensor Plate NO.1

s2.ptxt: Remove the crank angle sensor plate No.1 from the crankshaft.
Remove the bolt and remove the timing chain guide from the crank cap.
Remove the bolt and remove the chain tensioner slipper.
Remove the 2 bolts and remove the chain vibration damper No.1.
Remove the chain.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Crankshaft Timing Gear or Sprocket

s2.ptxt: Remove the crankshaft timing gear from the crankshaft.
Turn the crankshaft 90° counterclockwise, and align the fixing hole of the oil pump drive shaft with the fixing groove of the oil pump.

atten4.ptxt: Set the crankshaft pulley key horizontally to the left.

s2.ptxt: Insert a pin punch (diameter 3mm) into the fixing hole of the oil pump drive shaft gear to hold the gear, and remove the nut.
Remove the bolt, and remove the chain tensioner plate and damper spring.
Remove the oil pump drive gear, oil pump drive shaft gear and chain No.2.
Using a screwdriver wrapped with protective tape, remove the crankshaft pulley key and oil pump drive spline key from the crankshaft.
Remove the 4 camshaft bearing caps No.2 and No.3 in the order shown in the illustration.

atten3.ptxt: Uniformly loosen the bolts while keeping the camshaft level.

atten4.ptxt: Arrange the removed parts in order according to their installation positions.

s2.ptxt: Remove the camshaft No.2.
Remove the 4 camshaft bearing caps No.1 and No.3 in the order shown in the illustration.

atten3.ptxt: Uniformly loosen the bolts while keeping the camshaft level.

atten4.ptxt: Arrange the removed parts in order according to their installation positions.

s2.ptxt: Remove the camshaft.
Remove the camshaft bearing No.1 from the camshaft bearing cap No.1.
Remove the camshaft bearing No.2 from the cylinder head.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Camshaft Timing Gear or Sprocket

s2.ptxt: Secure the hexagonal service portion of the camshaft in a vise, with aluminum plates in between.
Remove the bolt and remove the camshaft timing gear.
Secure the hexagonal service portion of the camshaft in a vise with aluminum plates in between, and check that the camshaft timing gear assembly does not turn.
Cover all oil holes in the cam journal with vinyl tape, except for 1 hole (advance oil hole) in the position shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: Since 4 of the oil holes are inside a groove, cover only 3 hole using a piece of rubber.

s2.ptxt: Into the oil hole 150kPa{1.5kgf/cm2While applying approximately } of air pressure, force the camshaft timing gear assembly to rotate in the advance direction (counterclockwise).

atten3.ptxt: Cover with a shop rag, as oil may splash when air pressure is applied.

atten4.ptxt: Depending on the air pressure, the timing gear assembly may turn in the advance direction without applying force by hand. Also, if air leaks from the port and pressure is difficult to apply, the lock pin may be difficult to release.

s2.ptxt: Remove the flange bolt and remove the camshaft timing gear assembly.

item.ptxt: Slide the camshaft timing gear assembly horizontally off the camshaft to remove it.
When reusing the camshaft timing gear assembly, release the straight pin lock before use.

s2.ptxt: Using a double hexagon wrench (10mm), uniformly loosen the cylinder head bolts in 2-3 steps in the order shown in the illustration, and remove the 10 bolts and 10 plate washers.

item.ptxt: If the camshaft timing oil control valve is not removed, it may be damaged when loosening the cylinder head bolts.
Do not drop the plate washers into the cylinder head when removing the bolts.
Failure to follow the correct order may damage the cylinder head.

atten4.ptxt: Arrange the removed bolts and washers in order according to their installation positions.

s2.ptxt: Remove the cylinder head gasket from the cylinder head.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Cylinder Block Water Jacket Spacer

s2.ptxt: Using needle-nose pliers, remove the cylinder block water jacket spacer from the water jacket.

atten3.ptxt: When turning the cylinder block upside down, be sure to remove the water jacket spacer, as it will fall out.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Cylinder Block Water Drain Cock Sub-assembly

s2.ptxt: Remove the water drain cock plug from the water drain cock.
Remove the water drain cock from the stiffening crankcase.
Using a 8 socket hexagon wrench, remove the screw plug, and remove the oil control valve filter and gasket.

s-1.ptxt: Remove Plug NO.1 (w/ Head Taper Screw)

s2.ptxt: Remove the taper screw plug No.1 from the cylinder block.
Remove the 3 bolts, and remove the oil pump assembly and gasket.
Using a dial indicator, measure the thrust clearance of each balance shaft.

atten4.ptxt: If the clearance is more than the maximum, replace the balance shaft housing and bearing. If the thrust surface of the balance shaft is damaged, also replace the balance shaft.

s2.ptxt: Using a socket wrench (12mm), uniformly loosen the 8 balance shaft housing set bolts in several steps in the order shown in the illustration, and remove the balance shaft housing.

atten4.ptxt: Arrange the removed parts in order according to their installation positions.

s2.ptxt: Place a strip of Plastigage across the journal and install the balance shaft housing.
Apply a light coat of engine oil to the bolt seats.
Using a socket wrench (12mm), temporarily tighten the 8 balance shaft housing set bolts in several steps in the order shown in the illustration, then tighten them to the specified torque.

item.ptxt: Install the housing set bolts in their original positions.
Tighten the housing set bolts using the plastic region tightening method.

s2.ptxt: Mark the front of the housing set bolt heads with paint.
Using the paint marks as a guide, tighten each bolt an additional 90° in the tightening order.
Check that all paint marks have been turned 90° in the tightening direction.
Remove the balance shaft housing and measure the Plastigage at its widest point.

atten3.ptxt: After inspection, completely remove the Plastigage.

s2.ptxt: If the clearance is more than the maximum, select and replace the bearing.
Inspect Balance Shaft Housing Set Bolt

s3.ptxt: Using vernier calipers, measure the under-head length of the housing set bolts.

item.ptxt: If the length is more than the maximum, always replace the housing set bolt with a new one, as the engine may be damaged.
If the bolt threads are damaged, replace the housing set bolt.

s-1.ptxt: Remove No. No.1 and No. No.2 Balance Shafts

s2.ptxt: Remove the No. No.1 and No. No.2 balance shafts.
Remove the 8 balance shaft bearings No.1 from the stiffening crankcase assembly and balance shaft housing.
Using a utility knife, cut off the oil seal lip.
Using a screwdriver wrapped with protective tape, pry out the oil seal.

item.ptxt: After removing the oil seal, check that the crankshaft is not damaged.
If it is damaged, smooth it with sandpaper (#400).

s2.ptxt: Uniformly loosen and remove the 11 bolts in several steps in the order shown in the illustration.
Using a screwdriver wrapped with protective tape, pry at the locations shown in the illustration and remove the stiffening crankcase assembly.

atten3.ptxt: Do not damage the contact surfaces of the stiffening crankcase assembly and cylinder block.

s2.ptxt: Remove the O-ring from the cylinder block.
Using a spring scale, measure the length of the timing chain when it is pulled with a force of 140N{14.3kgf}.

atten3.ptxt: Perform the measurement at 3 or more places and use the average value.

atten4.ptxt: If the length is more than the maximum, replace the chain.

content1.ptxt: Using a spring scale, measure the length of the timing chain when it is pulled with a force of 140N{14.3kgf}.

atten3.ptxt: Perform the measurement at 3 or more places and use the average value.

atten4.ptxt: If the length is more than the maximum, replace the chain No.2.

s2.ptxt: Wrap the chain around the oil pump drive gear and, using vernier calipers, measure the outer diameter.

atten3.ptxt: The vernier calipers must contact the chain rollers when measuring.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is less than the minimum, replace the oil pump drive gear.

s-1.ptxt: Inspect Oil Pump Drive Shaft Gear

s2.ptxt: Wrap the chain around the oil pump drive shaft gear and, using vernier calipers, measure the outer diameter.

atten3.ptxt: The vernier calipers must contact the chain rollers when measuring.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is less than the minimum, replace the oil pump drive shaft gear.

s2.ptxt: Wrap the chain around the camshaft timing gear assembly and, using vernier calipers, measure the outer diameter.

atten3.ptxt: The vernier calipers must contact the chain rollers when measuring.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is less than the minimum, replace the camshaft timing gear assembly.

s-1.ptxt: Inspect Camshaft Timing Gear or Sprocket

s2.ptxt: Wrap the chain around the camshaft timing gear and, using vernier calipers, measure the outer diameter.

atten3.ptxt: The vernier calipers must contact the chain rollers when measuring.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is less than the minimum, replace the camshaft timing gear.

s-1.ptxt: Inspect Crankshaft Timing Gear or Sprocket

s2.ptxt: Wrap the chain around the crankshaft timing gear and, using vernier calipers, measure the outer diameter.

atten3.ptxt: The vernier calipers must contact the chain rollers when measuring.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is less than the minimum, replace the crankshaft timing gear.

s2.ptxt: Using vernier calipers, measure the dimension of the chain tensioner slipper shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: If the dimension is less than the minimum, replace the chain tensioner slipper.

s2.ptxt: Using vernier calipers, measure the dimension of the chain vibration damper No.1 shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: If the dimension is less than the minimum, replace the chain vibration damper No.1.

s2.ptxt: Using vernier calipers, measure the dimension of the chain tensioner plate shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: If the dimension is less than the minimum, replace the chain tensioner plate.

s2.ptxt: Using vernier calipers, measure the under-head length of the cylinder head bolts.

item.ptxt: If the length is more than the maximum, always replace the cylinder head bolt with a new one, as the engine may be damaged.
If the bolt threads are damaged, replace the cylinder head bolt.

s2.ptxt: With the cam lock released, push the plunger and check that it moves smoothly.

atten4.ptxt: If it does not move smoothly, replace the chain tensioner assembly No.1.

s2.ptxt: With the cam lock applied, check that the plunger does not move when pushed.
Runout Inspection

s3.ptxt: Using a dial indicator, measure the camshaft runout.

atten4.ptxt: If the runout is more than the maximum, replace the camshaft.

s2.ptxt: Height Inspection

s3.ptxt: Using a micrometer, measure the cam lobe height.

atten4.ptxt: If the height is less than the minimum, replace the camshaft.

s2.ptxt: Outer Diameter Inspection

s3.ptxt: Using a micrometer, measure the journal diameter.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is not as specified, check the oil clearance. (see )

s2.ptxt: Runout Inspection

s3.ptxt: Using a dial indicator, measure the camshaft runout.

atten4.ptxt: If the value is more than the maximum, replace the camshaft No.2.

s2.ptxt: Height Inspection

s3.ptxt: Using a micrometer, measure the cam lobe height.

atten4.ptxt: If the value is less than the minimum, replace the camshaft No.2.

s2.ptxt: Outer Diameter Inspection

s3.ptxt: Using a micrometer, measure the journal diameter.

atten4.ptxt: If the diameter is not as specified, check the oil clearance. (see )
